title: Retail Installment Contracts: Borrower Payoff Payments
content:
**Policy entry.** This rule fixes the amount a borrower pays to pay off an active contract under Retail Installment Contracts in full on the posting date with a payment made as a payoff, which closes the contract as paid off by the borrower.

**Conditions on the record.** A payoff payment is taken only after the contract's records carry a payoff statement quoted on the posting date. The payoff amount is not fixed until each returned payment on the contract that owes a returned-payment fee carries it.

## Capability

`authorize_payoff_payment_7f0b790b` is the borrower's own authorization of a payment from their own funds that pays the contract off in full today. One call posts a payoff payment dated today for the amount given: its principal portion clears the principal balance, its fee portion settles all fees due and the rest is its interest portion; the contract's balances go to zero, the contract is closed as paid off by the borrower, and the fee settlement is recorded. The borrower sees the payment and the closed contract.

## How it is invoked

This is the customer's own tool: the representative unlocks `authorize_payoff_payment_7f0b790b` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to authorize the payment.

## Parameters

- `contract_id` — the contract reference number of the retail installment contract being paid off, as returned by the contract lookup or quoted on the payoff statement; text identifier.
- `payment_channel` — how the borrower pays, one of: `ach_autopay` (drawn by the borrower's recurring automatic draft); `ach_self_service` (a one-time bank draft scheduled by the borrower through the phone line, website or app); `ach_agent` (the borrower gives a live representative their bank account for a one-time draft); `debit_card_self_service` (debit card through the phone line, website or app); `debit_card_agent` (the borrower gives a live representative a debit card); `moneygram` (a MoneyGram payment); `check_mail` (a mailed personal check); `wire_transfer` (a wire sent by the borrower's bank); `certified_funds` (a cashier's check or money order); `third_party_remittance` (an insurer, auction or other third party remits the funds); `not_applicable` (no payment channel applies — never for a payoff).
- `amount_usd` — the payoff amount paid, in USD with 2 decimal places, 0.00 or more; stored rounded half-up to the cent exactly as passed.

## Return

A receipt rendered as text with `contract_txn_id` (reference of the payoff payment), `contract_id`, `txn_date` (YYYY-MM-DD posting date), `amount_usd` (amount paid, 2 decimal places), `principal_applied_usd`, `fees_applied_usd` and `interest_applied_usd` (its portions, 2 decimal places), `status` (the text `paid_off`, meaning the contract is closed as paid in full) and `closed_date` (YYYY-MM-DD). A receipt carrying the payment reference and that status means the payoff has posted.
